| eval pivot="process"
| append [ search `web_logs` (url="*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*" OR url="*firedalazer*" OR uri_query="*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*" OR uri_query="*firedalazer*") | eval pivot="web" ]
| stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(process) as commands values(url) as urls by host user pivot
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: File or Process Matching Article Hash IOCs
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0b

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash

| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

[LLM] Check Point VPN IKEv1 authenticated session without machine certificate (CVE-2026-50751) Exploitation High
Hunts the exploitation primitive for CVE-2026-50751: Remote Access VPN / Mobile Access / Spark gateway sessions negotiated via the deprecated IKEv1 key exchange, on gateways not enforcing machine-certificate authentication. Surfaces the vulnerable configuration state being actively used and any successful IKEv1 logins from the article's external IPs. Rationale: Targets the exact preconditions named in the Check Point advisory: IKEv1 + no machine cert + legacy Remote Access clients. Anchors on the 8 article-confirmed source IPs to keep FPs near zero. Cross-checked against the CISA KEV listing for CVE-2026-50751 and Check Point's published mitigation guidance (IKEv2-only + mandatory Machine Certificate Authentication). Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://support.checkpoint.com/results/sk/sk183001
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Authentication.Authentication
// Defender does not natively ingest Check Point gateway logs; this pivots on inbound VPN egress traffic observed by onboarded endpoints to Qilin IPs that just authenticated via the Check Point appliance.

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (QilinIPs) or LocalIP in (QilinIPs)
| where RemotePort in (500, 4500, 443)  // IKE / IKE-NAT-T / SSL-VPN
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalIP, LocalPort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let QilinIPs = dynamic(["45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Check Point"
| where DeviceProduct in~ ("VPN-1 & FireWall-1","Mobile Access","Quantum Spark","SmartDefense","Security Gateway")
| where (Message has_any ("IKEv1","IKE_v1","Phase 1","Legacy Remote Access","SecuRemote") 
         or DeviceCustomString1 has_any ("IKEv1","Legacy Remote Access")
         or DeviceCustomString2 has_any ("IKEv1","Legacy Remote Access"))
| where DeviceAction in~ ("accept","Key Install","Log") or EventOutcome =~ "success"
| where SourceIP in (QilinIPs) or Message has_any (QilinIPs)

[LLM] Outbound EDR traffic to Check Point CVE-2026-50751 / Qilin affiliate infrastructure Command & Control High
Hunts any endpoint reaching out to the 8 IP indicators tied to Qilin affiliate exploitation of CVE-2026-50751 — catches both inbound exploit attempts replayed in flow telemetry and post-compromise C2/staging beacons from VPN-assigned internal hosts. Rationale: Eight article-confirmed IPs make this a clean IOC-pivot. Network-only detection avoids dependence on the Check Point appliance forwarding its logs. CloudWatch query left empty — Qilin C2 lives on Windows endpoints, not CloudTrail. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let QilinIPs = dynamic(["45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(45d)
| where RemoteIP in (QilinIPs)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Connections=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort), Procs=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName)
  by DeviceName, DeviceId, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by FirstSeen asc
let QilinIPs = dynamic(["45.77.149.152","209.182.225.136","38.60.157.139","162.33.177.101","45.76.26.42","144.208.127.155","38.54.88.201","38.54.107.167"]);

( CommonSecurityLog

( ImNetworkSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
  | where DstIpAddr in (QilinIPs) or SrcIpAddr in (QilinIPs)
  | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=EventVendor, Product=EventProduct, Src=SrcIpAddr, Dst=DstIpAddr, DstPort=DstPortNumber, User=SrcUsername, Action=DvcAction, Bytes=NetworkBytes )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Qilin affiliate payload hash execution / write (CVE-2026-50751 post-compromise) Installation High
Hunts for execution or file-write of the two MD5 hashes Check Point/CISA attributed to Qilin affiliate activity following CVE-2026-50751 VPN exploitation. High-fidelity IOC match across process, image-load, and file-write telemetry. Rationale: MD5s come directly from the article's IOC bundle and triangulate against the Qilin affiliate attribution Check Point published. Hash IOCs across process/file/image-load tables cover both staging and live execution paths. CloudWatch left empty — these are endpoint binaries, not CloudTrail-shaped. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1032/
ATT&CKT1486 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem

union isfuzzy=true
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(45d)
  | where MD5 in (QilinHashes) or InitiatingProcessMD5 in (QilinHashes)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ProcessExec", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, ProcessCommandLine, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine ),
( DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(45d)
  | where MD5 in (QilinHashes)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType=tostring(ActionType), FileName, FolderPath, MD5, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine ),
( DeviceImageLoadEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(45d)
  | where MD5 in (QilinHashes)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ImageLoad", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine )
| order by Timestamp desc
let QilinHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689","51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union isfuzzy=true
( SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where FileHash has_any (QilinHashes)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Account, FileHash ),
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
  | where MD5 in (QilinHashes) or Hash in (QilinHashes)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, NewProcessName=TargetProcessName, CommandLine=TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Account=ActorUsername, FileHash=MD5 ),
( ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
  | where TargetFileMD5 in (QilinHashes) or Hash in (QilinHashes)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, NewProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName="", Account=ActorUsername, FileHash=TargetFileMD5 )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Post-VPN-auth Qilin ransomware staging behavior on internal hosts Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the post-compromise activity Qilin operators perform after pivoting through a Check Point VPN tunnel: shadow-copy deletion, BCDedit recovery disablement, Defender tampering, and ESXi vmkfstools/vim-cmd invocation within minutes of a new VPN-pool logon. Stitches CommonSecurityLog VPN auth to endpoint behavior. Rationale: Stitches the article's exploit vector (Check Point VPN auth) to the named threat (Qilin RaaS) by joining VPN-assigned client logons to recovery-inhibition behavior within 2h — a tight time-window correlation that drops the FP rate well below a standalone vssadmin-delete query. Cross-checked Qilin TTPs against MITRE ATT&CK G1032 and prior public Qilin IR write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1032/ • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
ATT&CKT1490 T1562.001 T1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let WindowMin = 120m;
let VpnAuthHosts = DeviceLogonEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(45d)
    | where LogonType == "Network" or LogonType == "RemoteInteractive"
    | where RemoteIPType == "Private"  // VPN-pool client IPs are RFC1918
    | project AuthTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteIP;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(45d)
| where (FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("shadow","delete"))
     or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "shadowcopy" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete")
     or (FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe" and (ProcessCommandLine has "bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures" or ProcessCommandLine has "recoveryenabled" and ProcessCommandLine has "No"))
     or (FileName =~ "wbadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("catalog","systemstatebackup"))
     or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring","Set-MpPreference -DisableBehaviorMonitoring","Remove-MpPreference"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner VpnAuthHosts on DeviceName
| where Timestamp between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + WindowMin)
| project Timestamp, AuthTime, MinutesAfterAuth=datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, AuthTime), DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMin = 120m;
let VpnAuthHosts = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
    | where EventID == 4624
    | where LogonType in (3, 10)
    | where IpAddress startswith "10." or IpAddress startswith "192.168." or IpAddress matches regex @"^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\."
    | project AuthTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, IpAddress;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(45d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith "\\vssadmin.exe" and CommandLine has_all ("shadow","delete"))
     or (NewProcessName endswith "\\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "shadowcopy" and CommandLine has "delete")
     or (NewProcessName endswith "\\bcdedit.exe" and (CommandLine has "bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures" or CommandLine has "recoveryenabled" and CommandLine has "No"))
     or (NewProcessName endswith "\\wbadmin.exe" and CommandLine has "delete" and CommandLine has_any ("catalog","systemstatebackup"))
     or (NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has_any ("Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring","Set-MpPreference -DisableBehaviorMonitoring"))
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner VpnAuthHosts on Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (AuthTime .. AuthTime + WindowMin)
| project TimeGenerated, AuthTime, MinutesAfterAuth=datetime_diff('minute', TimeGenerated, AuthTime), Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, IpAddress
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:(4688 OR 1)) (@CommandLine:(*"shadowcopy delete"* OR *"shadows /all"* OR *"bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures"* OR *"recoveryenabled No"* OR *"DisableRealtimeMonitoring"* OR *"delete catalog"*)) (@Image:(*\vssadmin.exe OR *\VSSAdmin.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\WMIC.exe OR *\bcdedit.exe OR *\BCDEdit.exe OR *\wbadmin.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ((ImageFileName=/\\vssadmin\.exe$/i CommandLine=/shadow.*delete/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\wmic\.exe$/i CommandLine=/shadowcopy.*delete/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\bcdedit\.exe$/i CommandLine=/(bootstatuspolicy\s+ignoreallfailures|recoveryenabled\s+No)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\wbadmin\.exe$/i CommandLine=/delete.*(catalog|systemstatebackup)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i CommandLine=/Set-MpPreference.*Disable(Realtime|Behavior)Monitoring/i)) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50751", "CVE-2026-50752")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host

ImFileEvent

| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental

    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or SHA1 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce") or MD5 in~ ("52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["52fda5c1b9704544f32ee98d9060e689", "51d39aa39478beeac94f2d12f682ecce"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Inventory hunt that surfaces hosts still on Chrome versions older than 149.0.7827.102 (Windows/Linux) or 149.0.7827.103 (macOS), or with CVE-2026-11645 / -2441 / -3909 / -3910 / -5281 reported by the TVM/vuln scanner. [LLM] Cluster of Chrome renderer crashes via WerFault across multiple hosts Exploitation Medium
Alerts when WerFault.exe is spawned by chrome.exe at burst rates or across multiple distinct hosts within a short window — the heap-corruption signature of CVE-2026-11645 attempted exploitation (the article explicitly notes the bug can trigger a crash). Single user crashes are noise; clustered crashes against the same site visit pattern are exploitation telemetry. Rationale: Article explicitly states the V8 OOB R/W bug can 'trigger a crash' alongside info disclosure / RCE — burst crashes are the operationally observable phase. Pivot is WerFault parented by chrome.exe (article-specific to the Chrome process model), with threshold to suppress single-user noise. Cross-checked against: • https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/
ATT&CKT1499.004 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes

| where DistinctHosts >= 3 or CrashCount >= 10
| project FirstCrash, LastCrash, CrashCount, DistinctHosts, SampleDevices, SampleCmd
| order by FirstCrash desc

[LLM] chrome.exe spawning LOLBin child process (post-V8 sandbox escape) Installation High
Hunts for chrome.exe directly parenting cmd/powershell/mshta/regsvr32/rundll32/wscript/cscript/bitsadmin/certutil — the article's described arbitrary-code-execution-in-renderer outcome of CVE-2026-11645 manifests, after sandbox escape, as one of these LOLBin children. Chrome legitimately spawns only a small whitelist of children (chrome_crashpad_handler, software_reporter_tool, GoogleUpdate); anything else is high-fidelity. Rationale: Chrome's process tree is well-known and tightly bounded — any LOLBin child is high-signal regardless of cmdline. The article's specific claim of 'arbitrary code execution inside the web browser's sandbox' becomes operationally visible only when the renderer escapes and spawns one of these binaries. Cross-checked against: • https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/
ATT&CKT1203 T1059.001 T1218

[LLM] Chrome navigation to low-reputation domain immediately preceding renderer crash Delivery Medium
Time-window join surfacing the article's drive-by exploitation pattern: chrome.exe contacts an external URL (the 'crafted HTML page' delivery vector for CVE-2026-11645) and a renderer crash (WerFault parented by chrome.exe / Application Error 1000) follows on the same host within ~120 seconds. The pairing is the classic shape of a heap-corruption browser exploit attempt. Rationale: Article calls out the delivery primitive ('crafted HTML pages') and the impact primitive ('triggering a crash') as both being outputs of CVE-2026-11645; the high-fidelity signal is the temporal pairing of an external Chrome HTTP request and a renderer crash. ImWebSession + Event(EID 1000) is the cleanest Sentinel path that doesn't depend on Defender XDR ingestion. Cross-checked against: • https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1189/

[LLM] LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 MCP test endpoint POST (preview command injection) Exploitation High
Detects HTTP POSTs to LiteLLM's vulnerable MCP test endpoints (/mcp-rest/test/connection and /mcp-rest/test/tools/list) that accept full stdio server configurations and spawn arbitrary commands as the proxy user. Both endpoints are pre-patch attacker entrypoints called out by BerriAI and Horizon3.ai. Rationale: Both URIs are named verbatim in BerriAI's advisory and the article as the only two endpoints that accepted stdio command/args/env in the request body pre-1.83.7. Any POST to these paths is a high-fidelity exploit signal. Cross-checked Horizon3.ai write-up and BerriAI security advisory. Defender Advanced Hunting has no clean inbound-HTTP request table, so defender_kql left empty; primary surface is reverse-proxy / IIS / WAF logs (sentinel_kql + datadog_query). Cross-checked against: • https://www.horizon3.ai/ • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1190 T1059

| where csUriStem in~ (endpoints)
| where scStatus !startswith "4"   // exclude blocked / pre-auth 401
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent, scStatus, scBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc
@http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:("/mcp-rest/test/connection" OR "/mcp-rest/test/tools/list") -@http.status_code:[400 TO 499]

[LLM] LiteLLM proxy (uvicorn/python) spawning shell or LOLBin — CVE-2026-42271 post-exploit Installation High
Detects child processes spawned by the LiteLLM proxy process (python/uvicorn running litellm) where the child is a shell, network downloader, or recon binary inconsistent with normal LiteLLM operation. CVE-2026-42271 spawns the attacker-supplied command as a subprocess of the proxy process — this is the host-side fingerprint of successful exploitation. Rationale: BerriAI's advisory and the article both state the proxy 'spawned the supplied command as a subprocess on the proxy host with the privileges of the proxy process'. The parent process is therefore python/uvicorn running litellm.proxy. Any shell / curl / whoami child of that exact parent is the canonical post-exploit fingerprint and rare in normal LiteLLM operation. Cross-checked BerriAI advisory and Horizon3.ai analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://www.horizon3.ai/ • https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/security/advisories

[LLM] Anomalous Host header to LiteLLM (Starlette CVE-2026-48710 BadHost bypass) Exploitation Medium
Detects HTTP requests to LiteLLM that carry a Host header outside the deployment's baseline of expected hosts, especially when reaching auth-gated paths. CVE-2026-48710 abuses Starlette's host header validation so an attacker can submit a forged Host to bypass LiteLLM's auth and reach the vulnerable MCP test endpoints unauthenticated. Rationale: Horizon3.ai chained CVE-2026-48710 (Starlette BadHost) with CVE-2026-42271 to reach LiteLLM's MCP test endpoints unauthenticated, and the article's mitigation guidance explicitly calls out reviewing logs for 'unusual Host header activity'. The on-wire signature is a request whose Host header is forged or unexpected for the deployment. Defender / Falcon FDR don't ship HTTP request data so those fields are empty; primary surface is HTTP access logs. Cross-checked Horizon3.ai analysis and Starlette security advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://www.horizon3.ai/ • https://github.com/encode/starlette/security/advisories
ATT&CKT1190 T1078

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — cross-operator admin API key mint via POST /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys Exploitation High
Hunts the exact endpoint abused in exploit chain A — handleCreateOperatorAPIKey lacks any admin/ownership check pre-v0.3.4, so any successful POST to /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys by a non-admin actor mints a fresh bearer for an arbitrary operator (including admins). On an unpatched server this single request is privilege escalation. Rationale: Endpoint path /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys and the handleCreateOperatorAPIKey function at internal/api/operators.go:118 are quoted verbatim from the GHSA — exploit chain A delivers an admin bearer in one curl with no ownership check pre-v0.3.4. Successful POST on this exact path is the signal. No external corroboration available — CVE freshly minted (2026-47724) and GHSA is the authoritative source.
ATT&CKT1068 T1078.003 T1190
Data sourcesWeb
// Primary: W3CIISLog when nebula-mesh is fronted by IIS/Azure App Gateway. Adapt cs* fields for AppServiceHTTPLogs or CommonSecurityLog (RequestURL/RequestMethod) as needed.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/operators/[^/]+/api-keys/?$"
| where scStatus in (200, 201)
| extend TargetOperatorId = extract(@"/api/v1/operators/([^/]+)/api-keys", 1, csUriStem)
| extend CVE = "CVE-2026-47724"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, AuthUser=csUserName, csMethod, csUriStem, TargetOperatorId, scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, CVE
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — cross-tenant host identity hijack via /hosts/{id}/reenroll → /enroll chain Installation High
Detects exploit chain B: a single source POSTs to /api/v1/hosts/{id}/reenroll (mints a single-use enrollment token for an arbitrary host with no ownership check) then immediately POSTs to /api/v1/enroll with attacker-controlled X25519/Ed25519 keys, overwriting signing_pub_pem and the cert. Same-source temporal correlation within ~60s on these two specific paths is the textbook exploitation signature. Rationale: Both endpoints (/api/v1/hosts/{id}/reenroll and /api/v1/enroll) and the temporal chain are explicitly walked in the article (internal/api/hosts.go:321,330 → mintEnrollmentTokenForHost, then enroll.go:175 overwrites signing_pub_pem). The 60-second window is generous — exploit code typically chains these in <5s. Sigma skipped because this is multi-event temporal correlation that single-event Sigma can't express.
ATT&CKT1098.001 T1212 T1552.004 T1550.001
Data sourcesWeb
let Lookback = 7d;
let WindowSec = 60;
let Reenroll = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where csMethod == "POST"
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/hosts/[^/]+/reenroll/?$"
    | where scStatus in (200, 201)
    | extend VictimHostId = extract(@"/api/v1/hosts/([^/]+)/reenroll", 1, csUriStem)
    | project ReenrollTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUserName, VictimHostId, ReenrollAgent = csUserAgent;
let Enroll = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where csMethod == "POST"
    | where csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/enroll/?$"
    | where scStatus in (200, 201)
    | project EnrollTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, EnrollAgent = csUserAgent;
Reenroll
| join kind=inner Enroll on cIP, Computer
| where EnrollTime between (ReenrollTime .. ReenrollTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', EnrollTime, ReenrollTime)
| extend CVE = "CVE-2026-47724"
| project ReenrollTime, EnrollTime, DelaySec, Computer, cIP, csUserName, VictimHostId, ReenrollAgent, EnrollAgent, CVE
| order by ReenrollTime desc
source:nginx @http.method:POST (@http.url_details.path:/api/v1/hosts/*/reenroll OR @http.url_details.path:/api/v1/enroll) (@http.status_code:200 OR @http.status_code:201)

[LLM] nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — operator roster + API key metadata enumeration burst Reconnaissance Medium
Hunts the discovery phase of exploit chain A — a single source/bearer fanning out across GET /api/v1/operators and GET /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys (handleListOperators and handleListOperatorAPIKeys both lack admin gates per the GHSA) to identify admin operators and their key IDs before minting the privileged bearer. Rationale: Article enumerates the five operator-management handlers missing admin gates (operators.go:66 list, :79 disable, :94 enable, :157 revoke, :173 list-keys). Combining GET /api/v1/operators with multiple GET /api/v1/operators/{id}/api-keys in a short window is the natural recon shape before exploit A. Sigma skipped — threshold-based aggregation isn't expressible in single-event Sigma.
ATT&CKT1087 T1526 T1069.003

W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "GET"
| where scStatus == 200
| where csUriStem == "/api/v1/operators" or csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/operators/[^/]+/api-keys/?$"
| summarize DistinctPaths = dcount(csUriStem),
            RequestCount = count(),
            SamplePaths = make_set(csUriStem, 20),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),

          by cIP, csUserName, csUserAgent, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctPaths >= 3 or RequestCount >= 8
| extend CVE = "CVE-2026-47724"
| order by FirstSeen desc

[LLM] nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — cross-tenant firewall mutation via PUT /api/v1/networks/{id}/firewall Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects state-changing writes to nebula-mesh firewall configuration on the /api/v1/networks/{id}/firewall endpoint, which trusts bearer auth alone pre-v0.3.4 per exploit chain C. An attacker with cross-tenant API access can open or remove firewall rules in any network in the deployment. Rationale: Article calls out /api/v1/networks/{id}/firewall (get, PUT) as part of exploit chain C and the CVSS rationale flags 'Mass cross-tenant CRUD including firewall-rule mutation' as a primary impact. Writes (PUT/POST) are the high-fidelity slice; reads would be too noisy.

[LLM] nebula-mesh CVE-2026-47724 — operator sabotage (disable/enable/key revocation) by non-admin actor Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the impact phase of CVE-2026-47724 — handleDisableOperator (line 79), handleEnableOperator (line 94), and handleRevokeOperatorAPIKey (line 157) all lack admin gates per the GHSA. An exploited bearer can disable peer operators, re-enable disabled ones, or revoke any operator's API keys to lock legitimate admins out. Rationale: Article's 'Affected operator-management handlers' section explicitly lists each of these three handlers and their line numbers as missing admin gates. Disable/enable/revoke against a non-self target operator from a non-admin actor is unambiguous exploitation. Falcon, Defender, and CloudWatch all left empty: these are HTTP API calls to a custom Go server, not endpoint/AWS telemetry — only web-tier logs see them.
ATT&CKT1531 T1098 T1496
Data sourcesWeb
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where scStatus in (200, 201, 204)
| where (csMethod == "POST" and (csUriStem endswith "/disable" or csUriStem endswith "/enable") and csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/operators/[^/]+/(disable|enable)/?$")
     or (csMethod == "DELETE" and csUriStem matches regex @"^/api/v1/operators/[^/]+/api-keys/[^/]+/?$")
| extend TargetOperatorId = extract(@"/api/v1/operators/([^/]+)/", 1, csUriStem)
| extend Action = case(
    csUriStem endswith "/disable", "operator_disable",

| extend CVE = "CVE-2026-47724"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, AuthUser=csUserName, csMethod, Action, TargetOperatorId, csUriStem, scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, CVE
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] osascript invoked with AppleScript breakout pattern (mismatched tell blocks + do shell script) Exploitation High
Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-47252 in Anyquery: a SQL-controlled URL is interpolated unescaped into an AppleScript template and reaches `osascript -e`. The injected payload closes the original `tell application` block early, runs `do shell script`, then reopens a new `tell application` block — producing a command line containing both `end tell` and `do shell script` alongside two `tell application` openers. Rationale: Pulled the exact exploitation primitive from the PoC at tabs.go:141: the injected URL contains literal newlines that close one `tell application "Google Chrome"` block with `end tell`, runs `do shell script "id"`, then reopens a second `tell application` block. Detecting the co-occurrence of these three AppleScript tokens on an osascript command line — especially when spawned by anyquery — is a fingerprint of this CVE's exploitation. Cross-checked the GitHub advisory and the affected package paths (julien040/anyquery plugins/chrome, plugins/brave, plugins/edge, plugins/safari). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hrj8-hjv8-mgwc • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/002/
ATT&CKT1059.002 T1190

| where ProcessCommandLine has "end tell"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "tell application"
| extend TellOpeners = countof(tolower(ProcessCommandLine), "tell application")

   or InitiatingProcessFileName has "anyquery"

| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] External MS Teams chat invite from IT-impersonating unmanaged or federated tenant Delivery Medium
Hunts for inbound Microsoft Teams chat invitations from external/guest users whose display name or sender domain impersonates internal IT/helpdesk/MSP functions — the exact technique Cloaked Ursa and UNC6692 used to initiate the social-engineering conversation before requesting MFA approval. Rationale: Maps to the article's central narrative — external Teams chat from an unmanaged/federated tenant whose sender display name impersonates IT/helpdesk/MSP. Combines the external-user predicate (#EXT#/onmicrosoft.com/UserType=Guest) with the IT-impersonation lexicon Unit 42 calls out as the lowered-suspicion lure.

[LLM] MFA approval within minutes of inbound external Microsoft Teams chat Exploitation High
Correlates an inbound external Teams chat to a user with a successful MFA-satisfied sign-in by that same user inside a 30-minute window. Surfaces the Cloaked Ursa / UNC6692 pattern where the 'IT technician' chat is immediately followed by a victim-approved MFA push. Rationale: 30-minute window pairing an inbound external Teams chat with an MFA-satisfied sign-in by the same recipient maps directly to the article's narrative — 'IT technician' chat → 'approve this MFA' → compromise. Time-window correlation is the noise-killer the BluRaven kb prescribes for this scenario.
ATT&CKT1621 T1566.003
Data sourcesAuthentication
let WindowMinutes = 30m;
let ExternalChats = CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where Application =~ "Microsoft Teams"
    | where ActionType in~ ("ChatCreated","MessageSent","MemberAdded")
    | extend RawStr = tostring(RawEventData)
    | where AccountType in~ ("Guest","External") or RawStr has_any ("#EXT#","onmicrosoft.com")
    | extend Recipient = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ActivityObjects))[0].Name)
    | project ChatTime = Timestamp, SenderUpn = AccountDisplayName, SenderIP = IPAddress, Recipient, ActionType;
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where AuthenticationRequirement =~ "multiFactorAuthentication"
| extend AuthDetailStr = tostring(AuthenticationDetails)
| where AuthDetailStr has_any ("Mobile app notification","PhoneAppNotification","OAuth Verify","Authenticator App")
| join kind=inner ExternalChats on $left.AccountUpn == $right.Recipient
| where Timestamp between (ChatTime .. ChatTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelayMinutes = datetime_diff('minute', Timestamp, ChatTime)
| project ChatTime, MfaApprovalTime = Timestamp, DelayMinutes, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, Application, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, ConditionalAccessStatus, SenderUpn, SenderIP
| order by MfaApprovalTime desc

[LLM] Activity involving ommicrosoft.com Cloaked-Ursa Teams typosquat Delivery High
Direct IOC hunt for the ommicrosoft.com typosquat domain referenced by Unit 42 in connection with Cloaked Ursa / Midnight Blizzard Teams credential-harvesting infrastructure. Sweeps Teams/Office activity, AAD sign-ins, DNS resolutions, and proxy traffic for any reference to the domain. Rationale: ommicrosoft.com is the only hard IOC in the article — a single-character typosquat of microsoft.com that Unit 42 ties to Cloaked Ursa Teams credential-harvesting. Any resolution, web request, sign-in reference, or Teams artifact mentioning this string is high-fidelity. Union covers chat, sign-in, DNS, and proxy surfaces because the same domain may surface across all four during the kill chain.
ATT&CKT1583.001 T1566.003 T1656
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution Web Authentication
let IOC = dynamic(["ommicrosoft.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceNetworkEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where RemoteUrl has_any (IOC) or AdditionalFields has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="NetworkEvents", DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP),
    (UrlClickEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where Url has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="UrlClickEvents", DeviceName="", AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName="", RemoteUrl=Url, RemoteIP=tostring(IPAddress)),
    (CloudAppEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where Application =~ "Microsoft Teams"
        | extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData), Acts = tostring(ActivityObjects)
        | where Raw has_any (IOC) or Acts has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="Teams", DeviceName="", AccountUpn=AccountDisplayName, InitiatingProcessFileName=ActionType, RemoteUrl=ObjectName, RemoteIP=IPAddress),
    (AADSignInEventsBeta
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where AccountUpn has_any (IOC) or AlternateSignInName has_any (IOC) or ResourceDisplayName has_any (IOC)
        | project Timestamp, Source="AADSignIn", DeviceName=DeviceName, AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName=Application, RemoteUrl=ResourceDisplayName, RemoteIP=IPAddress)
| order by Timestamp desc
let IOC = dynamic(["ommicrosoft.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (OfficeActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where UserId has_any (IOC) or tostring(Parameters) has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="OfficeActivity", Operation, User=UserId, SrcIP=ClientIP, Detail=tostring(Parameters)),
    (SigninLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where UserPrincipalName has_any (IOC) or AppDisplayName has_any (IOC) or ResourceDisplayName has_any (IOC) or AlternateSignInName has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="SigninLogs", Operation=OperationName, User=UserPrincipalName, SrcIP=IPAddress, Detail=strcat(AppDisplayName," | ",ResultDescription)),
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where Name has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Operation=QueryTypeName, User="", SrcIP=ClientIP, Detail=Name),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationHostName has_any (IOC) or RequestURL has_any (IOC) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (IOC)
        | project TimeGenerated, Source="Proxy/CSL", Operation=DeviceAction, User=SourceUserName, SrcIP=SourceIP, Detail=coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PHPSpreadsheet phar:/// three-slash wrapper in HTTP request (CVE-2026-45034) Exploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests carrying the patch-bypass form 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' (three or more slashes after the scheme) used to evade PHPSpreadsheet's File::prohibitWrappers helper. The single-slash form 'phar://x/' is correctly rejected by the patch; the triple-slash variant is the live bypass that still reaches PHP's phar stream wrapper. Rationale: Targets the literal bypass fingerprint from the advisory: 'phar:///path/file.phar/inner' with three or more slashes after the scheme. The advisory explicitly contrasts the rejected single-slash 'phar://x/dummy.csv' (negative control) against the surviving triple-slash 'phar:///work/exploit.phar/dummy.csv' (positive control), so a regex of `phar:/{3,}` plus its URL-encoded form is the exact patch-bypass discriminator. Defender XDR has no native inbound HTTP request telemetry so defender_kql is left empty; the detection lives in web-server / WAF logs that ship to Sentinel, Splunk Web, or Datadog. Did not perform external web search — the GitHub Security Advisory is itself the authoritative source for this CVE.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesWeb
let bypass_pattern = @"(?i)phar:/{3,}|phar%3a%2f%2f%2f";
let wrapper_pattern = @"(?i)phar:/{2}|phar%3a%2f%2f";
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| extend FullUrl = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery)
| where FullUrl matches regex wrapper_pattern
| extend IsBypassVariant = iff(FullUrl matches regex bypass_pattern, "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = cIP, URL = FullUrl, UserAgent = csUserAgent, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, IsBypassVariant, LogSource = "W3CIISLog")
| union (CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL matches regex wrapper_pattern
| extend IsBypassVariant = iff(RequestURL matches regex bypass_pattern, "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, URL = RequestURL, UserAgent = RequestClientApplication, Method = RequestMethod, Status = tostring(EventOutcome), IsBypassVariant, LogSource = "CommonSecurityLog")
| where IsBypassVariant == "yes"   // 3+ slashes after scheme = patch bypass
| order by TimeGenerated desc
