[LLM] Web-server process (php-fpm / apache / nginx / w3wp) spawning shell or network tooling Exploitation Medium
Hunts post-exploitation behaviour following CVE-2026-45034 RCE on PHP 7.x — the phar metadata __wakeup/__destruct gadget runs inside the web-server worker, so the parent of any spawned shell/network LOLBin is php-fpm, apache2, httpd, nginx, or w3wp.exe. Article-specific because PHP web workers almost never legitimately spawn sh/bash/curl/wget/nc. Rationale: The advisory states the gadget chain runs '__wakeup' and '__destruct' on PHP 7.x 'inside the victim process' — meaning the PHP web worker. So the post-RCE pivot is the same web-worker process spawning anything that's not another PHP worker. Excluding php→php parents (legitimate FPM pool spawning) and constraining child to shell/network LOLBins narrows the FP surface. Marked hunting (not alerting) because legitimate apps do shell out from PHP for image/video processing. Did not perform external web search — the technical detail in the GitHub advisory was sufficient to write this detection.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe","nc","ncat","ncat.exe","socat","python","python3","python.exe","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName != "" and AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php.exe","php","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP / Web-Server Worker Spawning Shell or Network LOLBin (CVE-2026-45034 post-exploit)
id: 1c8e6a4d-2f5b-4a3e-9d7c-6b8a1f3e2c4d
description: Detects post-RCE behaviour where php-fpm, apache, nginx or w3wp spawn shell/network tools — the gadget chain in the CVE-2026-45034 patch bypass executes inside the web worker on PHP 7.x.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-87m4-826x-3crx
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_webworker:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php'
      - '/php-cgi'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/nginx'
      - '\php-fpm.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
  child_lolbin:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/socat'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/perl'
      - '/ruby'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
  condition: parent_webworker and child_lolbin
falsepositives:
  - Image processing pipelines (ImageMagick, ffmpeg) invoked via shell from PHP
  - Deployment / config-management agents shelling out from web context
  - Legitimate webhook handlers that exec system commands
level: medium
(source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon) AND @process.parent.name:(*php-fpm* OR *php.exe OR php OR *apache2* OR *httpd* OR *nginx* OR *w3wp.exe*) AND @process.name:(sh OR bash OR dash OR zsh OR cmd.exe OR powershell.exe OR pwsh.exe OR curl OR curl.exe OR wget OR wget.exe OR nc OR ncat OR socat OR python OR python3 OR perl OR certutil.exe OR bitsadmin.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(php-fpm|php|php-cgi|httpd|apache2|nginx|w3wp\.exe)$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|curl|wget|certutil|bitsadmin)\.exe$|\/(sh|bash|dash|zsh|curl|wget|nc|ncat|socat|python|python3|perl|ruby)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen), max(@timestamp, as=LastSeen), collect([CommandLine, UserName], multival=true)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe","nc","ncat","ncat.exe","socat","python","python3","python.exe","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| eval cve="CVE-2026-45034"
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.process_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe","nc","ncat","ncat.exe","socat","python","python3","python.exe","perl","ruby","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| eval cve="CVE-2026-45034"
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Phar archive or PHPSpreadsheet RCE marker written by web-server process Delivery Medium
Hunts for .phar files written into web-server-writable directories by a PHP/web-worker process (staging step of CVE-2026-45034) and for the PoC artefact file 'pwned_marker' that the published exploit drops on successful RCE. .phar uploads to web roots are extremely unusual outside of deliberate deployment. Rationale: Two article-specific strings drive this: '.phar' (the exploit archive extension referenced throughout the advisory — exploit.phar in the PoC) and 'pwned_marker' (the literal file the published gadget writes containing 'WAKEUP: phpspreadsheet-bypass' / 'DESTRUCT: phpspreadsheet-bypass'). Both must be written by a web-worker process, which is the parent constraint that turns it from a generic 'phar file appeared' dashboard into a CVE-tied detection. Did not perform external web search — the advisory contained sufficient detail.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","apache2","httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName endswith ".phar"
     or FileName =~ "pwned_marker"
     or FileName =~ "exploit.phar"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php.exe","php","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".phar"
     or TargetFileName =~ "pwned_marker"
     or TargetFileName =~ "exploit.phar"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Phar Archive or pwned_marker File Written by PHP / Web-Server Worker (CVE-2026-45034)

| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45034", "CVE-2026-34084")

NFCShare Android malware spreads via fake banking app updates on GitHub

BleepingComputer
2026-06-08 7 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

New variants of the NFCShare Android malware are being distributed as fake updates for legitimate banking apps hosted on GitHub. [...]

ATT&CKT1190 T1566

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] M365 URL click to GitHub repo hosting NFCShare banking-themed APK · [LLM] GitHub-sourced APK download with Italian/Spanish bank impersonation filename · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Android EDR: NFCShare WebSocket C2 from sideloaded banking-impersonating package · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] M365 URL click to GitHub repo hosting NFCShare banking-themed APK Delivery High
Hunts user clicks on URLs pointing to GitHub raw/release paths whose filename matches the NFCShare distribution APK names (Intesa Carte, Sella Carte, Nexi Carte, Fideuram, Mooney, CaixaBank, CaixaReactivaTarjeta). Catches the phishing→GitHub redirect step described by D3Lab. Rationale: Uses the verbatim 9 APK filenames from the article plus the GitHub hosting infrastructure described by D3Lab. The cross-join of (GitHub host) + (bank-themed APK filename) is an extremely tight predicate with very low FP rate for corporate web egress. Cross-checked against: • https://d3lab.net • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let SuspectFilenames = pack_array("Intesa Carte.apk","Sella Carte.apk","Banca Sella Carte.apk","Nexi Carte.apk","Fideuram Carte.apk","Mooney Carte.apk","CaixaBank.apk","CaixaBankNfc.apk","CaixaReactivaTarjeta.apk");
let GithubHosts = dynamic(["github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com","github.io","codeload.github.com"]);
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any (GithubHosts)
| where Url endswith ".apk" or Url has_any (SuspectFilenames)
| where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough","UrlScanInProgress")
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, NetworkMessageId, IPAddress, ActionType, ThreatTypes
| join kind=leftouter (EmailUrlInfo | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | project NetworkMessageId, UrlDomain, EmailUrl=Url) on NetworkMessageId
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectFilenames = dynamic(["intesa carte.apk","sella carte.apk","banca sella carte.apk","nexi carte.apk","fideuram carte.apk","mooney carte.apk","caixabank.apk","caixabanknfc.apk","caixareactivatarjeta.apk"]);
let GithubHosts = dynamic(["github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com","github.io","codeload.github.com"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| extend UrlLower = tolower(Url)
| where UrlLower has_any (GithubHosts)
| where UrlLower endswith ".apk" or UrlLower has_any (SuspectFilenames)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, EventVendor
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GitHub-sourced APK download with Italian/Spanish bank impersonation filename Delivery High
Hunts file-create events on managed endpoints (BYOD-sync folders, mobile-management staging, USB transfer hosts) where an APK matching the NFCShare distribution filename list lands and the file-origin URL is GitHub. Catches the second step (download) when the click event itself wasn't captured. Rationale: The 9 APK filenames are verbatim IOCs from D3Lab's tracking of the GitHub repo (created 2026-04-10, 56 APKs total). Pinning on filename + browser/email parent process is a high-fidelity drop signal even when the proxy log misses the URL. Cross-checked against: • https://d3lab.net • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1105/
ATT&CKT1105 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let SuspectFilenames = pack_array("Intesa Carte.apk","Sella Carte.apk","Banca Sella Carte.apk","Nexi Carte.apk","Fideuram Carte.apk","Mooney Carte.apk","CaixaBank.apk","CaixaBankNfc.apk","CaixaReactivaTarjeta.apk");
let GithubHosts = dynamic(["github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","objects.githubusercontent.com","github.io","codeload.github.com"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".apk"
| where FileName has_any (SuspectFilenames) or FileOriginUrl has_any (GithubHosts) and FileName endswith ".apk"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","outlook.exe","teams.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, FileName, FolderPath, FileOriginUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectFilenames = dynamic(["intesa carte.apk","sella carte.apk","banca sella carte.apk","nexi carte.apk","fideuram carte.apk","mooney carte.apk","caixabank.apk","caixabanknfc.apk","caixareactivatarjeta.apk"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| extend FnLower = tolower(TargetFileName)
| where FnLower endswith ".apk"
| where FnLower has_any (SuspectFilenames)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Android EDR: NFCShare WebSocket C2 from sideloaded banking-impersonating package Command & Control Medium
On Android-MDM / Mobile-Threat-Defense telemetry shipped to SIEM, hunts apps installed outside Play Store whose package label matches the NFCShare cluster (Carte / Carta / Tarjeta / Nfc) AND that subsequently open outbound WebSocket connections (port 80/443 ws/wss) to non-CDN hosts. Targets the exfil step described: 'exfiltrates card PAN/expiry/PIN over a WebSocket channel'. Rationale: Combines the article's specific bank-impersonation naming convention (the 9 listed APKs all use Carte/Carta/Tarjeta tokens) with the explicit WebSocket exfil protocol called out in the body. Constrains to Android telemetry so the corporate-Windows noise floor doesn't fire. Cross-checked against: • https://d3lab.net • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1437/001/
ATT&CKT1437.001 T1521
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where OSPlatform == "Android" | distinct DeviceId, DeviceName) on DeviceId
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("Carte","Carta","Tarjeta","CaixaBank","Reactiva","Nexi","Sella","Intesa","Fideuram","Mooney")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("websocket","\"upgrade\":\"websocket\"","ws://","wss://")
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hosts = make_set(RemoteUrl, 20) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by FirstSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DeviceProduct has_any ("Intune","Lookout","Zimperium","Pradeo","Defender for Endpoint")
| where ApplicationProtocol in~ ("websocket","wss","ws")
| where SourceUserName has_any ("Carte","Carta","Tarjeta","CaixaBank","Reactiva","Nexi","Sella","Intesa","Fideuram","Mooney")
   or DeviceCustomString1 has_any ("Carte","Carta","Tarjeta","CaixaBank")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceHostName, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol, DeviceCustomString1
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(mobile.defender OR intune OR lookout OR zimperium) (@app.name:(*Carte* OR *Carta* OR *Tarjeta* OR *CaixaBank* OR *Reactiva* OR *Nexi* OR *Sella* OR *Intesa* OR *Fideuram* OR *Mooney*)) AND (@network.protocol:(websocket OR ws OR wss) OR @http.upgrade:websocket)

ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),

| order by conn_count desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Hades Campaign: install of trojanized scientific PyPI packages (ensmallen 0.8.101 et al.) Delivery High
Detects pip/poetry/uv installing the specific compromised versions of ensmallen, embiggen, gpsea, pyphetools, mflux-streamlit, nhmpy, or ppkt2synergy named in the Hades Campaign advisory. Also catches the PyPI/pythonhosted.org artifact download for those exact package-version filenames so a side-channel pip wrapper is still caught. Rationale: Pivots on the exact (package,version) pairs called out as compromised in the article — these strings are unique enough that any positive hit is high-fidelity. The network half catches sidecar installers that don't emit a clean pip command line by matching the artifact filename PyPI hosts (e.g. ensmallen-0.8.101-*.whl on files.pythonhosted.org).
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","pip","pip3","poetry.exe","poetry","uv.exe","uv","python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3") or FileName in~ ("pip.exe","pip3.exe","poetry.exe","uv.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesPkgs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| union (DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has "pythonhosted.org" or RemoteUrl has "pypi.org"
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (HadesArtifacts)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl)
| order by Timestamp desc

| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("pip","poetry","uv","python")
| where CommandLine has_any (HadesPkgs)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| union (CommonSecurityLog

  | where DestinationHostName has_any ("pythonhosted.org","pypi.org") or RequestURL has_any ("pythonhosted.org","pypi.org")
  | where RequestURL has_any (HadesArtifacts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, Account=SourceUserName, NewProcessName="", CommandLine="", ParentProcessName="", RequestURL)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Python process downloading Bun runtime v1.3.14 ZIP from oven-sh GitHub release Delivery High
Detects the Hades Campaign delivery step: an obfuscated import hook in a trojanized PyPI package's __init__.py reaches out to github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.14/bun-{linux,darwin,windows}-{x64,aarch64}.zip and writes the ZIP to a temp directory. This deliberately bypasses Node.js / package-manager controls. Rationale: The article quotes the exact URL `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.14/bun-{_m}-{_a}.zip` constructed in the deobfuscated Python hook — pinning v1.3.14 and pairing it with a python-process initiator makes this near-zero-FP. A legit Bun user would normally invoke the official install script, not fetch the ZIP from a Python parent.

[LLM] Bun runtime executed from /tmp/b or %TEMP%\b with Python parent (Hades Campaign loader) Installation High
Detects the Hades Campaign loader stage: a python process (from a trojanized PyPI package's import hook) spawning the newly-downloaded `bun` runtime out of /tmp/b/bun (Linux/macOS) or %TEMP%\b\bun.exe (Windows) with `run _index.js` to execute the AES-GCM-encrypted JavaScript payload bundle. Rationale: Triple-anchored on (a) the binary name `bun`, (b) the exact temp subdirectory `b/` the deobfuscated hook creates with `os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_b), exist_ok=True)`, and (c) the literal `_index.js` argument from `subprocess.run([_b, "run", _j], ...)`. Each one alone would have FPs; the conjunction is article-unique.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.006 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
| where (FolderPath has @"\Temp\b\" or FolderPath startswith "/tmp/b/" or FolderPath matches regex @"^/var/folders/.+/b/bun$")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","pythonw")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "run" and ProcessCommandLine has "_index.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\bun.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/bun"
| where NewProcessName has "\\Temp\\b\\bun" or NewProcessName has "/tmp/b/bun"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","\\python","/python")
| where CommandLine has "_index.js" and CommandLine has " run "
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| union (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/bun" or ActingProcessName endswith "\\bun.exe"
    | where ActingProcessName has "/tmp/b/" or ActingProcessName has "\\Temp\\b\\"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3","pythonw")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "_index.js" and ActingProcessCommandLine has " run "
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, NewProcessName=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Process reading /proc/<pid>/mem or accessing Runner.Worker for credential scraping Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Hades Campaign cross-platform memory scraper that reads GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process memory to extract plaintext secrets. On Linux it walks /proc/<pid>/maps and reads /proc/<pid>/mem; on Windows it calls OpenProcess/VirtualQueryEx/ReadProcessMemory against Runner.Worker; on macOS it calls task_for_pid via ctypes against the runner. Rationale: Anchors on the article's quoted Linux scraper behavior (`walks the memory mappings in /proc/{pid}/maps and directly reads /proc/{pid}/mem`) and macOS ctypes call `task_for_pid` invoked against TARGET_PID = Runner.Worker. On Windows the Sysmon EID 10 angle catches the OpenProcess/ReadProcessMemory primitive Phase 5 of the kill chain names. /proc/*/mem reads by python/bun are essentially never legitimate.
ATT&CKT1003 T1552.001 T1057

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath startswith "/proc/" and FileName in ("mem","maps"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","bun","node")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType
| union (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (runners) or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (runners)
    | where FileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","bun.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("task_for_pid","mach_vm_read","ReadProcessMemory","VirtualQueryEx","OpenProcess","ctypes.CDLL","/proc/")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType)
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] Hades GitHub C2 dead-drop: api.github.com commit search for magic keywords Command & Control High
Detects the three parallel GitHub-abused C2 channels of the Hades Campaign. Operators publish payloads in public commits tagged with the magic keywords DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom (token dead-drop), TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime (RSA-PSS-signed base64 JS), and firedalazer (signed Python URLs polled by updater.py). Infected hosts retrieve them via api.github.com/search/commits queries containing those keywords. Rationale: The three magic keywords are quoted verbatim in the article's C2 phase as the dead-drop beacons (`DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom`, `TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime`, `firedalazer`) and combined with `api.github.com` they form a fingerprint with essentially no legitimate baseline — these are attacker-coined strings.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1567.001
Data sourcesWeb Endpoint.Processes
let HadesKeywords = dynamic(["DontRevokeOrItGoesBoom","TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
| where RemoteUrl has_any (HadesKeywords)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP
| union (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesKeywords)
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (HadesKeywords)

[LLM] Hades Campaign updater.py persistence dropper written by Bun or Python child Installation High
Detects the Hades Campaign persistence step: the `firedalazer` C2 dropper writes a Python script literally named `updater.py` to disk and registers it as a background service / scheduled task / launchd / systemd unit that polls GitHub hourly. The file is written by a bun or python child of the original trojanized-package import chain. Rationale: The article explicitly names the persistence artifact: `The malware writes a Python script named updater.py (blob vF202) to disk and installs it as a background service.` The combination of the literal filename `updater.py` + a bun/python/node parent process + a follow-on service/cron/launchd registration of that same script is a tight, article-specific fingerprint.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType
| union (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("sc.exe","schtasks.exe","systemctl","launchctl","crontab","systemd-run")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "updater.py"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType="PersistenceRegister")
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bun","python","pythonw","node")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType
| union (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("sc.exe","schtasks.exe")
    | where CommandLine has "updater.py"
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername=Account, ActingProcessName=NewProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=CommandLine, TargetFilePath="", TargetFileName="updater.py", EventType="PersistenceRegister")
| union (Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d") or SHA1 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d") or MD5 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d") or SHA1 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d") or MD5 in~ ("c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

One-Character Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Local Root Access, Exploits Now Public

The Hacker News
2026-06-08 10 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Security researchers have published a detailed, working exploit for a Linux kernel use-after-free that lets an unprivileged local user escalate to root and break out of a container. The flaw, CVE-2026-23111, sits in the kernel's nf_tables packet-filtering code and was patched upstream on February 5, 2026. Exodus Intelligence released its full technical walkthrough on June 8, and it is not even

[LLM] Unprivileged user namespace + nf_tables manipulation chain (CVE-2026-23111 exploitation) Exploitation High
Hunts the prerequisite sequence for CVE-2026-23111 exploitation on Linux: a non-root user creating a new user namespace (unshare -U / clone with CLONE_NEWUSER) and then driving nft inside it to manipulate nf_tables. The Exodus and FuzzingLabs PoCs both require this exact chain because nf_tables is otherwise unreachable to unprivileged users. Rationale: Article explicitly names the prerequisite combo: `nf_tables plus unprivileged user namespaces`. The PoC chains unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)→nft to reach the vulnerable nf_tables code path. Detecting the two-step within a tight window is far higher fidelity than alerting on either alone. Cross-checked against Ubuntu USN-7XXX advisory and Exodus Intel write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-23111 • https://www.exodusintel.com/ • https://fuzzinglabs.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/
ATT&CKT1068 T1611
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let NsCreate = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "unshare" or FolderPath endswith "/unshare"
    | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s|^)-(U|rU|Ur|Urm|-user)(\s|$)"
    | where AccountName != "root" and isnotempty(AccountName)
    | project NsTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, NsCmd = ProcessCommandLine, NsParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
let NftRun = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "nft" or FolderPath endswith "/nft"
    | project NftTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, NftCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
NsCreate
| join kind=inner NftRun on DeviceId, AccountName
| where NftTime between (NsTime .. NsTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NftTime, NsTime)
| project NsTime, NftTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, AccountName, NsCmd, NftCmd, NsParent
| order by NsTime desc

let WindowMinutes = 10m;
let NsCreate = ImProcessCreate

    | where ActorUsername != "root" and isnotempty(ActorUsername)
    | project NsTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, NsCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, NsParent = ParentProcessName;
let NftRun = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where DvcOs has "Linux"
    | where ActingProcessName endswith "/nft" or ActingProcessName == "nft"
    | project NftTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, NftCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine;
NsCreate
| join kind=inner NftRun on DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| where NftTime between (NsTime .. NsTime + WindowMinutes)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NftTime, NsTime)
| project NsTime, NftTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, NsCmd, NftCmd, NsParent

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*\/unshare OR \/usr\/bin\/unshare OR \/bin\/unshare) @process.command_line:(*\ -U* OR *--user* OR *-rU* OR *-Ur*) -@user.name:root -@user.id:0
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\/unshare$/i OR ImageFileName="unshare")
| CommandLine=/(\s|^)-(U|rU|Ur|Urm|-user)(\s|$)/
| UserName!=root

| eval delay := NftTime - _time
| delay >= 0 AND delay <= 600
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function={collect([ImageFileName, CommandLine, NftCmd, delay])})

[LLM] nft (nftables) ruleset manipulation by non-root account on Linux endpoints Exploitation Medium
Hunts direct invocations of `nft` performing add/create operations on tables, chains, sets, maps or rules by a non-root user. CVE-2026-23111 lives in nf_tables and is triggered by crafted nft ruleset operations from within a user namespace; legitimate nft management is overwhelmingly root-owned. Rationale: Article anchors the vulnerability in nf_tables ruleset processing, and both public PoCs (Exodus and FuzzingLabs) drive the bug via nft from inside a user namespace. Legitimate nft management is overwhelmingly root or systemd-launched — non-root invocations with state-changing verbs are a high-signal pivot specific to this CVE class. Cross-checked against MITRE T1562.004 and the FuzzingLabs Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 writeup. Cross-checked against: • https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-23111 • https://fuzzinglabs.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
ATT&CKT1068 T1562.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "nft" or FolderPath endswith "/nft"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("add table", "create table", "add chain", "create chain", "add set", "add map", "add rule")
| where AccountName != "root" and isnotempty(AccountName)
| where AccountSid != "S-1-5-18"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcOs has "Linux"
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/nft" or ActingProcessName == "nft"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("add table", "create table", "add chain", "create chain", "add set", "add map", "add rule")
| where ActorUsername != "root" and ActorUsername != "0" and isnotempty(ActorUsername)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Linux assets carrying vulnerable kernel for CVE-2026-23111 (nf_tables UAF) Reconnaissance High
Inventory hunt for Linux hosts still running a kernel package vulnerable to CVE-2026-23111. The fix shipped upstream 5 Feb 2026 and per-distro on varying dates; public PoCs have been out since 16 Apr. This UC surfaces exposure surface so patching is prioritised before an in-the-wild use of the bug emerges. Rationale: Article gives a clear CVE ID, fixed-version timeline (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/25.10, Debian Bookworm/Trixie+Bullseye LTS 6.1 backport, RHEL 10) and public-PoC dates. A posture query keyed on CVE-2026-23111 in Defender TVM yields the exposure surface a SOC needs to prioritise before threat-actor adoption. Cross-checked against Ubuntu USN tracker and Red Hat CVE database. Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc
